name: Chamonix Sud / Town Centre
tagline: Lively pedestrian heart of the valley
description: The bustling core, with the pedestrian streets, shops, restaurants and apres-ski bars, plus the Aiguille du Midi cable car nearby. Everything is walkable, the buzz is real in season, and it is the most convenient, if priciest, base for nomads.
bestFor: Nomads wanting walkable amenities, buzz and lift access without a car
pros: Best choice of bars and restaurants
Closest to the Aiguille du Midi lift
cons: Noisy and crowded in peak season

name: Les Praz de Chamonix
description: A pretty village just north of town, famous for its golf course, chalet character and stunning views of the Drus and Grands Montets. Quieter and more scenic than the centre, with an easy bus or short drive into Chamonix proper.
bestFor: Those wanting chalet charm, views and quiet within reach of town
pros: Close to Flegere and Grands Montets lifts
Good short bus ride to town

name: Les Pelerins / Les Bossons
tagline: Quieter valley base toward the tunnel
description: Residential villages southwest of the centre, near the Bossons glacier and the road to the Mont Blanc tunnel. More down-to-earth and often better value, with the valley train and bus giving easy access into Chamonix for work and play.
bestFor: Budget-minded longer stays wanting calm and good transport links
pros: Handy for the Mont Blanc tunnel road

name: Argentiere
tagline: Higher village at the Grands Montets
description: A characterful village up the valley at the foot of the Grands Montets ski area, popular with serious skiers and mountaineers. It sits higher and colder, holds snow well, and offers a tight-knit, outdoorsy community a short train ride from Chamonix.
bestFor: Committed skiers and mountaineers wanting altitude and snow-sure terrain
